title: AI Essentials: ChatGPT, Gemini & Copilot for Everyday Work
subtitle: Use ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Copilot with confidence to save hours on email, documents, research, spreadsheets, meetings and job hunting.
description:
This is a practical, beginner-friendly course for anyone who wants to use AI assistants in real daily work, without any technical background. If you are a working professional, a fresher, a career returner, someone moving from government-exam preparation to a private job, or a small business owner, this course is built for you.

You will learn how AI assistants like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Microsoft Copilot actually work, where they make mistakes, and how to choose the right one for each task. Then you will apply them to everyday work: drafting emails and messages in English, Hindi and regional languages, writing reports, researching and summarising long PDFs with proper fact-checking, working with spreadsheets, and turning meetings into clear action items.

The final module focuses on your career and habits: tailoring your resume and cover letter to real job posts, improving your LinkedIn profile, practising Indian-style interviews, and using AI safely within workplace privacy rules. You finish by building a personal library of 20 tested prompts and a weekly AI workflow plan.

Every lesson is short, written in plain English with Indian examples, and ends with a hands-on exercise you can complete in 10 to 20 minutes using free versions of the tools.
audience: Working professionals who want to save time on email, documents and reports
Freshers and graduates preparing for their first private-sector job
Career returners, including women restarting after a career break
Government-exam aspirants moving into private jobs
Small business owners and freelancers handling their own communication and admin
outcomes: Explain in plain words how AI assistants work and where they are likely to be wrong
Choose between ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Copilot based on the task and your tools
Write clear prompts that produce usable emails, reports and messages on the first or second try
Draft and translate messages in Hindi and regional languages with the right tone and register
Research a topic and summarise long PDFs while checking facts against original sources
Use AI for spreadsheet formulas, meeting minutes and action items

A free account on at least one AI assistant such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude or Copilot
No coding or technical background needed
tools: Google Workspace (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive, Meet)
projects: Build a personal prompt library of 20 tested, reusable prompts for your own work.
Create an AI-tailored resume and cover letter for a real job post you want to apply for.
Write a one-page research brief from three verified sources on a topic that matters to you.
Design a weekly AI workflow plan with anchor tasks, daily routines and a two-week tracker.

faqs.q: Do I need any technical or coding knowledge?
faqs.a: No. The course is written for non-technical learners. If you can use email and a web browser, you can follow every lesson and exercise.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay for ChatGPT, Gemini or Copilot?
faqs.a: No. You can complete every exercise with the free versions of these assistants. Some features inside Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace depend on your employer's or your own plan, and the lessons show you what to do if you don't have them.
Yes. A certificate of completion is issued once you have marked every lesson in the course as complete.
You can get a full refund within 7 days of purchase, as long as you have completed less than 30% of the course.

faqs.q: Is this course useful if I am returning to work after a career break?
faqs.a: Yes. The course was designed with career returners in mind. Module 5 specifically covers presenting a career break honestly on your resume, updating your LinkedIn profile and practising interview answers, and the earlier modules help you get comfortable with the AI tools many workplaces now use.

faqs.q: How long will it take to finish?
faqs.a: The course has 18 short lessons totalling about 7 hours, including exercises. Most learners finish comfortably in two to three weeks by doing one lesson a day, and you keep access to revisit lessons later.
